name: macaulay2-language-server
description: Macaulay2 language support powered by m2-ls

macaulay2.server.path.description: Path to m2-ls. Leave empty to use the bundled server or m2-ls from PATH.

macaulay2.trace.server.description: Trace communication between VS Code and m2-ls.

macaulay2.diagnostics.enabled.description: Show diagnostics. When disabled, no diagnostic is reported.

markdownEnumDescriptions: `X01`: Source the grammar cannot parse.
`X02`: A token the grammar expected but did not find, such as an `if` that ends after `then`.
`X03`: `L.1` reads as `L` applied to the float `.1`, not as member access; the fix suggests `L#1`.

`X04`: A parallel assignment target M2 cannot assign. Targets are assigned component-wise and may be symbols, nested lists, parts such as `x#i` (with `=`), or installation targets such as `T + T` or `f ZZ`; under `:=` an operator target must be an installation, so a literal operand rules it out.
`X05`: `:=` used to assign a part; parts are assigned with `=`.
`X06`: A parallel assignment whose two sides list different numbers of elements.
`S01`: A lowercase option key in a call; Macaulay2 option names are capitalized.
`S02`: A local binding that is never read. Names starting with `_` are exempt.
`S03`: Parentheses around a condition, `try` value, or loop range that the keyword already delimits.
`S04`: A null test that `??` expresses directly; here `x ?? 0`.
`S05`: An `if` or `try` with a shorter equivalent form: a redundant `null` branch, a negated condition, or a nesting that flattens into an `else if` chain.
`S06`: A multi-character ring variable such as `x0`, which is a separate symbol rather than the indexed variable `x_0`.

`E01`: A method installed on something that does not dispatch to it: a plain function rather than a `method()`, the binary form of `??`, or a `<-` method for anything but one non-symbol type. M2 evaluates `x <- v` by assigning a symbol `x` directly and otherwise calling the one-type method of `class x`, yet `installMethod` accepts every other domain.
`E02`: A method installed on an operator form Macaulay2 does not let users extend.
`E03`: A method function whose parameter count differs from the installed domain.
`E04`: A method installed with `=`, which Macaulay2 rejects; installations use `:=`.
`E05`: `protect x` on a bound name protects whatever symbol `x` evaluates to; `protect symbol x` protects `x` itself.
`E06`: `protect` applied to an expression, so the protected symbol is only known at run time.
`E08`: `return`, `break`, or `continue` outside the function or loop it needs.

`E09`: `x <- y` used as an assignment target, alone or inside a parallel assignment. That never installs a callable method, so it is always an error; `<-` is overloaded only with `installMethod(symbol <-, Type, function)`.
`T01`: A parallel assignment whose right side has a type that cannot supply several values.
`T02`: An `if` or `while` condition whose type is known not to be `Boolean`.
`T03`: A method installation without a codomain where inference can deduce one; the fix inserts `ZZ =>` here.
`T04`: A method installation whose declared codomain contradicts the inferred result type.
`syntax-error`: Source the grammar cannot parse.
`missing-node`: A token the grammar expected but did not find, such as an `if` that ends after `then`.
`ambiguous-float-member-access`: `L.1` reads as `L` applied to the float `.1`, not as member access; the fix suggests `L#1`.

`multiple-assignment-targets`: A parallel assignment target M2 cannot assign. Targets are assigned component-wise and may be symbols, nested lists, parts such as `x#i` (with `=`), or installation targets such as `T + T` or `f ZZ`; under `:=` an operator target must be an installation, so a literal operand rules it out.
`colon-equal-part-assignment`: `:=` used to assign a part; parts are assigned with `=`.
`parallel-assignment-arity`: A parallel assignment whose two sides list different numbers of elements.
`option-key-convention`: A lowercase option key in a call; Macaulay2 option names are capitalized.
`unused-binding`: A local binding that is never read. Names starting with `_` are exempt.
`redundant-control-parentheses`: Parentheses around a condition, `try` value, or loop range that the keyword already delimits.
`prefer-coalescence`: A null test that `??` expresses directly; here `x ?? 0`.
`simplifiable-expression`: An `if` or `try` with a shorter equivalent form: a redundant `null` branch, a negated condition, or a nesting that flattens into an `else if` chain.
`ring-variable-naming`: A multi-character ring variable such as `x0`, which is a separate symbol rather than the indexed variable `x_0`.

`install-no-effect`: A method installed on something that does not dispatch to it: a plain function rather than a `method()`, the binary form of `??`, or a `<-` method for anything but one non-symbol type. M2 evaluates `x <- v` by assigning a symbol `x` directly and otherwise calling the one-type method of `class x`, yet `installMethod` accepts every other domain.
`operator-not-flexible`: A method installed on an operator form Macaulay2 does not let users extend.
`install-arity`: A method function whose parameter count differs from the installed domain.
`install-needs-colon-equals`: A method installed with `=`, which Macaulay2 rejects; installations use `:=`.
`protect-assigned-symbol`: `protect x` on a bound name protects whatever symbol `x` evaluates to; `protect symbol x` protects `x` itself.
`protect-computed-symbol`: `protect` applied to an expression, so the protected symbol is only known at run time.
`invalid-control-transfer`: `return`, `break`, or `continue` outside the function or loop it needs.

`explicit-install-required`: `x <- y` used as an assignment target, alone or inside a parallel assignment. That never installs a callable method, so it is always an error; `<-` is overloaded only with `installMethod(symbol <-, Type, function)`.
`parallel-assignment-type`: A parallel assignment whose right side has a type that cannot supply several values.
`condition-type`: An `if` or `while` condition whose type is known not to be `Boolean`.
`install-codomain-missing`: A method installation without a codomain where inference can deduce one; the fix inserts `ZZ =>` here.
`install-codomain-mismatch`: A method installation whose declared codomain contradicts the inferred result type.

macaulay2.diagnostics.disabled.markdownDescription: Diagnostics to hide, by name (e.g. `unused-binding`) or code (e.g. `S02`).

macaulay2.formatting.indentWidth.markdownDescription: Spaces per indentation level. Leave unset to use the editor's indentation.

macaulay2.formatting.useTabs.markdownDescription: Indent with tabs. Leave unset to use the editor's indentation.

macaulay2.formatting.softLineWidth.markdownDescription: Line width the formatter prefers to wrap at. `0` disables preferred wrapping.

macaulay2.formatting.hardLineWidth.markdownDescription: Line width the formatter always wraps at. `0` disables forced wrapping.

enumDescriptions: Leave control flow on the lines it is written on.
Start each clause (then, else, do, list, …) and each body on its own line.
Like multiline, but keep the final else value on the else line.
macaulay2.formatting.controlFlowLayout.description: Layout of if/then/else expressions and loops.

macaulay2.formatting.compactFactorOperat.markdownDescription: Write factor operators without spaces, e.g. `2*x` instead of `2 * x`.

macaulay2.formatting.breakAfterSemicolon.description: Start the expression after a semicolon on a new line.

macaulay2.inlayHints.expressionTypes.description: Show the types of arguments, subexpressions, and call results.

macaulay2.inlayHints.allKnownTypes.description: Also show types that are obvious from literals.

scripts.test: npm run compile && npm run compile:test && node dist/test/runTests.js
